ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-59-1 and L. 561-45 to L. 561-53 (AML/CFT and beneficial owner declaration, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); Décret n° 2017-1147 du 7 juillet 2017 as amended by Décret n° 2023-641 (RBE filing conditions, 25% direct or indirect capital or voting-rights threshold); Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Loi Sapin II); Loi n° 2020-1508 du 3 décembre 2020 (AMLD5 transposition adjustments); Loi n° 68-678 du 26 juillet 1968 (French Blocking Statute) restricting compliance with foreign extraterritorial sanctions discovery; Code de commerce Articles L. 123-1 et seq. and R. 123-223 et seq. (RCS registration and company records); transposition of EU Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843, with forward alignment to EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1624.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_description: The French RBE is accessible to TRACFIN, ACPR, AMF, judicial authorities, notaries, bailiffs and all AML-obliged entities performing customer due diligence; public access is restricted to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest following CJEU Case C-37/20 and Article L. 561-47 CMF.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certified French translation; for non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization by the French embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, embassy, or registered agent in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign notarial copies; alternatively notarized photocopy verified by French counsel (copie certifiée conforme)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic execution by private deed or notarial act; no apostille required for French-origin documents; foreign-language annexes require certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, managers, and UBOs against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and related implementing acts), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and national French asset-freezing arrêtés issued by the Ministry of the Economy. PEP identification follows CMF Article L. 561-10 and EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 definitions; foreign PEPs and family members receive enhanced due diligence including documented source-of-funds analysis. OFAC SDN screening is applied solely as an operational overlay for USD-denominated payment clearing, strictly subordinate to the EU and French Blocking Statute, and is not a French statutory obligation.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.regulatory_filing_pipeline: Upon incorporation, the Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs must be filed electronically with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the INPI Guichet unique within 15 days; non-filing triggers a formal injunction and administrative fine under Article L. 561-47 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle; RCS availability verified against the national companies register maintained by the Greffes des Tribunaux de Commerce via the INPI Data and Infogreffe databases.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Latin script for entry in the RCS; non-Latin names (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew) require a Latin-script transliteration mandatory under Article R. 123-5 Code de commerce. French language is compulsory for all statutory instruments and pre-incorporation declarations (Article L. 121-1 Code de la consommation; Loi du 4 août 1994 relative à l'emploi de la langue française). The name must be licit (ordre public), distinctive within the relevant business sector, and must not infringe prior trademarks, trade names, or RCS-protected denominations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: FINANCE (where it implies regulated banking or credit activity)
FRANCE (where it falsely suggests public-sector affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_note: France does not maintain a statutory pre-incorporation name reservation register for companies; the 30-day window corresponds to the professional validity standard adopted by counsel for the pre-incorporation name-clearance opinion issued after RCS and trademark availability searches. A trademark application (depôt de marque) at INPI may also be filed pre-incorporation and affords protection for 10 years once granted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: 1. Upon name rejection, file a revised name through the INPI Guichet unique within 15 days at no additional statutory fee. 2. If the revised name is again rejected, lodge a summary application (référé) before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce under Article R. 123-166 Code de commerce within one month of the notification of refusal. 3. Engage counsel; standard hearing is obtainable within 12-15 business days. 4. Where refusal is grounded on a third-party trademark, pursue opposition or relative-ground cancellation before INPI under Articles L. 712-4 et seq. Code de la propriété intellectuelle. 5. Claim damages against the registry only upon proof of fault under Articles 1240-1241 Code civil.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_framework: Article L. 123-10 Code de commerce requires a registered office (siège social) stated in the articles; domiciliation at the legal representative's private residence is limited to 2 years (Article L. 123-11), while domiciliation at a licensed commercial domiciliation company is permitted for up to 6 years with mandatory declaration under Article L. 123-11-1.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted and commercially standard for the AIGC video SaaS industry. The SARL may be domiciled at a licensed société de domiciliation throughout the maximum 6-year term, renewable upon declaration and extension of the domiciliation contract. The virtual office must be a verifiable postal and official-notice address supporting the RCS record and the UBO file. No physical presence, retail space, or local client attendance is required by the governing regulations for ISIC 6201 software activities; however, the company should retain the domiciliation agreement, service contracts, and substance documentation (bank account, manager mandate, GDPR representation under Article 27 GDPR, French-language privacy policy and terms of service) to withstand anti-abuse and permanent establishment scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 8% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Greffier, DGFiP or URSSAF at the registered office; probability increases to 25% where the domiciliation host shelters more than 16 concurrent companies or where annual invoicing exceeds EUR 750,000 in the first fiscal year without full-time French-resident staff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 100 flat combining public-registry screening and structured search; official RCS search fee is zero, trademark search is optional at EUR 190 per class (none required at this stage)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of French-language Articles of Association (Statuts) and corporate formalities pack for a single-member or multi-member SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff: EUR 1,000-1,400 flat for standard SARL drafting, estimated 6-10 hours at EUR 130-180 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and UBO identification report: shareholder ownership tree, source-of-funds declaration, PEP and EU/UN/FATF sanctions screening of all individuals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance provider or AML officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 400-450 flat for a low-risk single-layer shareholder structure without non-cooperative-jurisdiction exposure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign-issued documents (certificate of incorporation, powers of attorney, identity documents, proof of address) for up to 6 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariffs of the issuing authorities plus French consular fees: EUR 20-80 per apostille and EUR 30-100 per consular legalization; total estimated EUR 330-370

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign-language documents by a traducteur assermenté listed with a Cour d'appel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement with a licensed French commercial domiciliation company, year-one fee incl. setup and pro-rata pre-incorporation term

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 40-70 per month on a 12-month contract plus EUR 50-150 setup; estimated EUR 580-640 for year one

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la société (Articles of Association) and Déclaration de création d'entreprise
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for SARL; capital may be set to a symbolic amount or zero
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The initial Board of Directors of the Company, convened and acting unanimously, resolves as follows: (1) To subscribe to the initial share capital of the Company in the amount of one hundred euros (EUR 100), represented by one hundred (100) shares of EUR 1 each; (2) To adopt the registered office at [full address], France; (3) To appoint [Full Name] as the sole Manager (Gérant) of the Company, vested with all powers of administration and representation; (4) To approve the draft Articles of Association (Statuts) and authorize their filing with the commercial registry; (5) To empower the Manager to complete all incorporation formalities and related filings. This resolution is adopted in compliance with the French Commercial Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Relance; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; business-registry and tax-initiation portal via the INPI Guichet Unique (formalités@inpi.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity needing a French tax identification number must file an RCS company registration (for an established permanent establishment or branch) through the Guichet Unique, or use the non-resident VAT registration procedure with the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) handling non-established suppliers. Where the foreign entity has no PE and only makes taxable supplies in France, it must register as a non-established taxable person for TVA purposes and may be required to appoint an accredited tax representative (représentant fiscal) if it is established outside the EU and receives B2C supplies requiring French VAT collection. The DGFiP issues the SIREN/SIRET and the individual TVA intra-community identification number (FR + 11 digits).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no generic check-the-box election in France. A SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level. Under CGI Article 239 bis AA, a SARL can elect for fiscal transparency (taxation in the hands of individual shareholders) if all shareholders are natural persons and no corporate member remains; the election is made by notification before the due date of the first profit-making year and is irrevocable for five years. For cross-border hybrid mismatch treatment, France applies the ATAD anti-hybrid rules (CGI Art. 212 bis, 209 B and 209 C) and no separate hybrid mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic established SARL: no mandatory VAT registration below the franchise thresholds of EUR 85,000 annual turnover for goods and EUR 37,500 for services; once those thresholds are exceeded, VAT registration is mandatory. Non-established foreign supplier: no de minimis threshold; any taxable supply in France triggers a French VAT registration obligation unless a special scheme (OSS/IOSS) applies or the supply is reverse-charged to a French business customer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured electronic invoicing for all domestic B2B transactions under the 2022 Finance Law reform, with phased applicability beginning 1 September 2026 for large and mid-sized enterprises and 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises. Invoices must flow through a registered dematerialization partner (PDP) or the public invoicing portal (Portail Public de Facturation), with structured data transmitted to the DGFiP. B2C transactions require e-reporting of transaction data to the DGFiP. There is no transactional real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system; compliance is based on periodic VAT returns and e-invoicing data analytics.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for the VAT zero rate (exonération) under CGI Article 262 ter I, provided the goods physically leave the EU within the statutory timeframe and the exporter retains proof of exit. Digital services, including AI video synthesis and virtual avatar generation SaaS, supplied to non-EU customers are outside French VAT where the customer is established or has his usual residence outside the EU (B2B place-of-supply rule under CGI Art. 259, and B2C electronic services under the destination principle). For B2C digital services to EU consumers, French VAT may apply unless OSS is elected.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration certified by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (SAD via DELTA)
Commercial invoice with explicit zero-rating reference
Bill of Lading / air waybill or other international transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU
Proof of payment or inward remittance from the non-EU buyer
Intra-community sales list and EU exporter summary report (where applicable) for goods moving under the Union Customs Code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where documentation is missing or the customs export proof is not obtained within the statutory period, the DGFiP reassesses output VAT at the standard or reduced rates applicable at the date of supply, and charges late-payment interest (intérêt de retard). In case of deliberate intent to evade or conceal tax, the penalty is 40% of the understated tax (mauvaise foi); where fraud is established or where the taxpayer has engaged in abusive practices, the penalty rises to 80% (manœuvres frauduleuses). Criminal prosecution for tax fraud (fraude fiscale) can impose imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to EUR 375,000, plus additional judicial penalties and publication of sanctions. Clawback periods follow the general French limitation rules of three years for annual VAT assessments, extending to six or ten years in cases of fraud or serious cross-border non-disclosure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) is the central bank with authority over balance-of-payments statistics, cash management, and the right-to-an-account mechanism; prudential oversight of credit institutions and payment institutions is delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); foreign-exchange control policy is administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) within the framework of EU Treaty provisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member with full and unrestricted euro convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions under Articles 63 through 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Council Directive 88/361/EEC. There are no exchange-control approval requirements for the SARL to export AI-avatar video-generation SaaS subscriptions, receive USD licensor or distribution fees, or remit dividends to non-resident shareholders. The only statutory friction points are tax-related, not FX-related: distribution of profits to non-resident individual shareholders is subject to the 30% flat withholding rate (prélèvement forfaitaire unique, PFU) absent treaty relief, while corporate shareholders resident in the EU/EEA may benefit from the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) where the 10% participation condition is met. Additionally, the SARL must comply with balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligations to the Banque de France for direct investment flows and with EU sanctions screening under Regulation (EU) 269/2014, Regulation (EU) 833/2014, and subsequent restrictive-measure packages.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion ratio exists in France for export proceeds or SaaS subscription receipts. The SARL may lawfully retain, hold, or freely convert USD and other foreign currency proceeds through French banks or the interbank FX market without prior Banque de France authorization. The only compulsory obligations are (i) EU cash-control declaration under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 for physical movements of cash or bearer instruments exceeding EUR 10,000, and (ii) cross-border balance-of-payments statistical reporting to Banque de France for transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 per operation or periodic consolidated filings where applicable. Invoicing in USD, EUR, or any freely convertible currency is permitted; no conversion quota applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for EU/EEA-authorized e-money institutions and payment institutions that are passportable into France under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2) and Directive 2009/110/EC (EMD2), including Qonto S.A. (ACPR-licensed French payment institution), Wise Europe SA (BSP-licensed, passporting), Airwallex, and Revolut Ltd (Lithuanian e-money license, EU passport); MEDIUM-LOW for offshore EMIs domiciled outside the EEA. Offshore non-EEA EMIs cannot lawfully provide payment or e-money services to a French-resident SARL without a French branch authorization or a passport, are not covered by the Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution (FGDR), and pose account-freeze and sanctions-screening risks. Recommended structure: primary transactional banking with a tier-1 French commercial bank; fintech EMIs used only as secondary settlement sub-rails for B2B disbursements and currency conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under French AML/CFT rules (Code monétaire et financier, arts. L.561-5 et seq. and ACPR prudential guidelines), the bank must identify the SARL, each gérant/director, and all ultimate beneficial owners declared in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE). Tier-1 French commercial banks generally require at least one physical identity interview with the appointed gérant at a French branch; remote onboarding via digital identity and video KYC may be conditionally accepted for the gérant and for shareholders holding less than 25% of capital, but non-resident UBOs holding 25% or more will typically be required to provide certified passport copies, apostilled proof of identity, source-of-wealth questionnaires, and a notarized board resolution. Fully remote account opening is available only through ACPR-regulated fintechs such as Qonto; traditional full-scope credit institutions seldom open SARL accounts without at least one in-person or consular meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: non-resident shareholders or an AI-software business where the bank cannot readily map control to a natural person.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current K-bis extract (less than 3 months old); RBE registration certificate; shareholders' register; notarized corporate resolution appointing the gérant; certified passports and proof of address for each UBO; source-of-wealth bank statements for the preceding 36 months; shareholder loan agreements if any; corporate diagram signed by the gérant; PEP status declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived deepfake/content-integrity risk: revenue model built on synthetic avatars triggers misuse-screening by compliance officers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product EULA and terms of service expressly prohibiting impersonation, deepfake fraud, and unlawful content; GDPR data protection impact assessment (DPIA); AI Act transparency documentation; technical watermarking and provenance-labeling policy; customer due-diligence policy for enterprise and wholesale clients; list of key enterprise customers; auditor comfort letter confirming that the licensing model is genuine software-as-a-service revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment aggregation concentration: large recurring volumes settled through Stripe and Paddle without direct contractual invoices being visible to the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe and Paddle; payment-settlement statements matched to SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit entries; sub-ledger of subscription receipts; downloadable customer invoicing records; reconciliation report signed by the statutory auditor; confirmation that the bank account is the exclusive payout destination.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin capitalization and rapid capital churn: low initial share capital followed by frequent non-EU investor wires or intercompany transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share capital deposit certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds); blocked capital escrow attestation; cash-flow forecast for 24 months; intercompany loan agreements priced at arm's length with supporting transfer-pricing documentation; shareholders' equity contribution deeds; explanation of angel/VC round structure; commitment not to transact with sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscriber inflow originating from high-risk or partially sanctioned jurisdictions, atypical for an EU SaaS issuer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geo-IP filtering and jurisdiction block-list logs; real-time sanctions screening report of counterparties; EU OFSI/OFAC list check outputs; dated export-control assessment classifying the AI-avatar software as non-sensitive under Regulation (EU) 2021/821; officer attestation of refusal of sanctioned customers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the SARL's equity injection, the first step is opening a blocked capital escrow account at a French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, then executing a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank with remittance information clearly stating 'Apport en numéraire – souscription au capital social – SARL [legal name]'. No FX authorization is required for EUR or USD wires; a non-EU shareholder sending EUR must include its own institution's compliance documentation such as source of funds and authorization from the capital-receiving country. Under France's foreign direct investment screening regime (art. L.151-3 CMF), prior authorization from the French Treasury is required only if a non-EU/ETA investor acquires control of, or obtains 25% of voting rights in, an entity active in strategic sectors including AI and robotics; otherwise, a qualifying inbound direct investment must be reported to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. The gérant must provide source-of-wealth declarations, the depository bank's attestation that the funds are blocked pending registration, and the draft articles of association.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) are the primary clearing rails for all EU/EEA supplier and refund disbursements; non-EU vendor payments, cloud-computing capacity purchases, and subcontractor fees are executed via SWIFT MT103 with structured remittance data (invoice number, purchase-order reference, and purpose text). Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are legally available and accepted by all tier-1 French banks but are commercially unsuitable for recurring AI-avatar SaaS licensing; they should be reserved for one-off high-value hardware or perpetual-license transactions. All outbound payments are subject in-house to sanctions screening, single-transaction limits set by the ACPR-licensed credit institution, and confirmation against the platform's refund and intercompany settlement schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward (marché à terme de devises) with a tenor up to 24 months under an uncommitted treasury line
EUR/USD FX swap (swap de devises) executed on the spot/forward pair for short-term rollover management
Cross-currency interest rate swap between EURIBOR and USD SOFR for hedged intercompany loan exposure
